title: The Eucharistic fast
hookLine: one hour without food before communion

lines: A GRANOLA BAR AND A CLOCK.
cards: Sunday, a quarter past nine. Mass is at ten. In the kitchen, someone reaches for a granola bar, stops, glances at the clock on the stove, and does a bit of arithmetic.
Communion comes partway through, so is there time? Coffee, yes or no? A glass of water is fine, isn't it?
It's a small, slightly comic moment, repeated in Catholic kitchens on Sunday mornings: grown adults doing math about a granola bar. But under the math is something serious.
Why would the Church ask anyone to go a little hungry before receiving bread?

teach.b: First, the rule, from the Church's law: someone who is going to receive the Eucharist abstains from all food and drink for at least one hour before communion.
Before communion, not before Mass, so the clock runs to the moment you receive, not to the opening hymn. Second, what's allowed.

The same law sets aside water and medicine; neither breaks the fast. And it adds something gentle: the elderly, the sick and the people who care for them may receive communion even if they've eaten within the hour.
The rule bends toward the people who need it to bend. Third, why.

Jesus says in John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger." The fast lets the body take part in that sentence. A little emptiness makes the bread stand out.
It marks this food as different from breakfast, and gives a short stretch, in the car, in the pew, to want what you're about to receive. Last, how small it is.
One hour isn't heroic, and that's partly the point: it's a fast sized for families with toddlers, for shift workers, for anyone.
Because it's small, it's easy to forget, which is why the granola-bar arithmetic happens at all.

teach.h: HE THAT COMETH TO ME SHALL NOT HUNGER.
teach.b: And the question under the arithmetic is a good one. Am I coming to this hungry? Or full, and distracted, and not really expecting anything?

how: Catholics in the Latin Church abstain from food and drink, except water and medicine, for at least one hour before receiving communion. The elderly, the sick and those caring for them are excused.

o: no food or drink for an hour before communion
a full day without food before First Communion
eating only bread on the day you receive communion

games.q: the Eucharistic fast — tap the pairs.
p: at least one hour before communion
may receive even if they've eaten
he that cometh to me shall not hunger

s: the hour is counted from the start of Mass
the law counts the hour before communion, not before Mass.
a glass of water breaks the Eucharistic fast
the law sets aside water and medicine.
people caring for the sick may receive communion even if they ate within the hour
the law excuses the elderly, the sick and those who care for them.

games.q: you're visiting your mother in a care home, and you ate a sandwich with her twenty minutes ago. a minister arrives with communion. what does Church law say?
o: you have to decline: it hasn't been an hour.
you may receive: those who care for the sick are excused from the hour.
you may receive only if you skip the sandwich next time.
games.why: the law that sets the hour also excuses the elderly, the sick and the people who care for them. the rule bends toward the people who need it to.

practice: Notice your body: is there any hunger in it, or thirst? Don't fix it; just notice where it sits, then ask what you're hungry for underneath the food: rest, company, forgiveness, quiet, a sense that things will be all right.
If you pray, offer that hunger to God; if you don't, stay with it, kindly, a little longer.

wordCard.voice: The Eucharistic fast. No food or drink for at least an hour before communion, with water and medicine allowed, and the sick, the elderly and their caregivers excused. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, the Eucharistic fast, as Church documents name it.

carryVoice: Your line: hungry for him. An hour of wanting, before the bread. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger
